records.summary: 921 Folsom St is in the MUR zoning district within the SoMa Youth and Family Special Use District, which requires Conditional Use Authorization for any restaurant use. The records show no prior applications at this exact address or parcel. The immediate block is moderately active with four food/drink businesses within 500 ft and four active ABC licenses (one Type 47, one Type 41, two off-sale). Within 1,000 ft there are only two dated Planning decisions in the last 10 years—too few to establish an approval rate—but both were approved: one CUA for a restaurant with a Type 41 license at 276 5th St (229 days, approved 2018) and one agency referral for a limited restaurant continuation.

flags.flag: Inside the SoMa Youth and Family Zone Special Use District, which requires Conditional Use Authorization for any restaurant use regardless of the underlying zoning designation.
The concept is a change of use from limited restaurant to restaurant, requiring Planning Department zoning referral and likely a building permit with change-of-use review.
No records on file at 921 Folsom St; the site history is blank, so there is no evidence of prior restaurant operations, permits, or ABC licenses at this address.
Four active ABC licenses within 500 ft: one Type 47 at 917 Folsom (21 m), one Type 41 at 276 5th St (76 m), and two off-sale licenses at 330 5th St and 301 5th St.
The CUA at 276 5th St for an Asian bowl restaurant with Type 41 license took 229 days from filing to approval (April 2018 to November 2018).
Adjacent properties at 915-917 Folsom St (21 m) have active restaurant uses with a Type 47 license and a history of Entertainment Commission permits for nighttime entertainment, indicating the block…
Also inside the Central SoMa Special Use District and Priority Equity Geographies SUD; these may offer fee waivers or streamlined review for certain projects.
Too few comparable decisions within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years (N = 2) to calculate a meaningful approval rate; the two decided cases were both approved.

data_gaps: No hearing transcripts or staff reports extracted for the 276 5th St CUA, so the specific conditions and community concerns are unknown.
No records explain why the Youth and Family SUD was drawn to include this block or what the Commission's posture is toward new restaurant CUAs here.
The existing use at 921 Folsom is stated as 'limited restaurant' in the concept profile, but no DPH permit or Planning record confirms that use is active or grandfathered.
ABC does not publish conditions for the Type 47 and Type 41 licenses nearby, so undue-concentration or crime-district findings are not visible.
The two comparable decisions are too few and too varied (one CUA, one continuation referral) to predict timeline or conditions for a new restaurant CUA.

comparables.why_comparable: CUA for a new restaurant with Type 41 beer-and-wine license at 276 5th St (51 m), MUR zoning within the same SoMa Youth and Family SUD. Change of use from vacant to restaurant, decided in November 2018.
comparables.key_takeaway: This is the only decided CUA in the candidate pool and the only comparable requiring a Commission hearing. It was approved in 229 days (April to November 2018), demonstrating that restaurant uses with alcohol in the Youth and Family SUD are approvable through CUA. The concept does not serve alcohol, which shortens the path, but the SUD still triggers CUA for any restaurant use.

comparables.why_comparable: Agency referral at the same 276 5th St address (51 m), MUR and Youth and Family SUD. Approved a limited restaurant in July 2018, three months before the CUA for the full restaurant with alcohol at the same site. Filed after the CUA was in process.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning noted 'On-site sale of alcohol requires CUA per SUD,' confirming that the Youth and Family SUD imposes CUA on alcohol service but not on dry restaurant uses. This concept serves no alcohol, so if the use is already established the change might be treated as continuation under Section 841 rather than a new CUA.

comparables.why_comparable: Health department referral for restaurant at 917 Folsom St (21 m next door), MUR zoning, approved March 2020 in 27 days. An agency referral approving continuation of restaurant use on the same block.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referrals for continuation of existing restaurant use in MUR are approved quickly (under 30 days). However, this is an agency referral, not a use decision; it tells us the site next door has operated as a restaurant but says nothing about whether a CUA would be required or approved for a new change of use at 921 Folsom.

comparables.why_comparable: Agency referral at 917 Folsom (21 m), MUR zoning, approved August 2015. Transfer of Type 47 full-bar license for restaurant with catering, approved per Sections 841.45 and 841.81 as principally permitted.
comparables.key_takeaway: Restaurant uses with alcohol licenses at 917 Folsom were approved as agency referrals (not CUAs) in 2015, before the Youth and Family SUD was mapped or before its rules were consistently applied. This suggests the immediate block has a multi-year track record of restaurant and alcohol use, but those approvals predate current SUD enforcement.

comparables.why_comparable: Health referral at 915 Folsom (21 m), MUR, approved February 2018 in 6 days as 'permitted use / not a change of use under PC 841,' meaning continuation of existing restaurant.
comparables.key_takeaway: Another continuation approval on the same block, processed as an agency referral in under a week. The record confirms the immediate Folsom Street frontage has multiple established restaurant uses, which may support a finding that this use is consistent with the existing character of the corridor.

comparables.why_comparable: Agency referral for restaurant (DNA Pizza) at 917 Folsom (21 m), MUR, approved October 2015 in 7 days per Section 841.45.
comparables.key_takeaway: Restaurant use at 917 Folsom approved as principally permitted in 2015. Multiple overlapping approvals at 915-917 Folsom show that site has cycled through several restaurant permits and operators, all approved without CUA hearings at that time.

comparables.why_comparable: Health referral for new restaurant at 212 6th St (292 m), NCT-SOMA zoning, approved February 2020 in 52 days. Notes BPA approval and Section 311 neighborhood notice completed.
comparables.key_takeaway: A new restaurant in a nearby neighborhood commercial district required a building permit alteration (BPA) with Section 311 notice but no CUA, because restaurants are principally permitted in NCT-SOMA. In contrast, the Youth and Family SUD at 921 Folsom imposes CUA even though MUR normally permits restaurants.

comparables.why_comparable: DPH referral for limited restaurant in MUR (address not shown but 107 m), approved October 2020 in 22 days as continuation of existing use per Section 841.
comparables.key_takeaway: Continuation of limited restaurant use in MUR approved quickly as an agency referral. The speed suggests Planning treats Section 841 continuation cases as ministerial when the use is not abandoned, but a change from limited to full restaurant may not qualify as continuation.

patterns.pattern: The SoMa Youth and Family Special Use District requires Conditional Use Authorization for restaurant uses with on-site alcohol service. One CUA for a restaurant with Type 41 license in the SUD was approved in 229 days; agency referrals explicitly noted alcohol requires CUA.

All decided restaurant applications within 300 m of 921 Folsom in MUR zoning since 2015 were approved, whether as CUA (N=1) or agency referrals for continuation or license transfers (N=6). No denials or withdrawals appear in the record.

Restaurant continuation approvals under Planning Code Section 841 in MUR are processed as agency referrals in under 30 days when the use is not abandoned. A change from limited restaurant to full restaurant may or may not qualify as continuation.

The immediate block (915-917 Folsom) has a multi-year history of restaurant and alcohol licenses, including Type 47 full-bar and Type 58 catering permits approved without CUA hearings in 2015, before consistent SUD enforcement.

New restaurant uses in nearby NCT-SOMA (principally permitted zoning) required building permit alteration approval and Section 311 neighborhood notice but no CUA. In MUR within the Youth and Family SUD, restaurants face stricter discretionary review.

risk.concept_summary: A 1,800 sq ft restaurant with full cooking (no alcohol service) at 921 Folsom St in San Francisco's MUR district, converting from limited restaurant use, with tenant improvements, exterior signage and five employees.

overall.next_step: Confirm in writing with Planning whether the change from limited restaurant to restaurant qualifies as continuation under Section 841 or requires a Conditional Use Authorization hearing under the Youth and Family SUD, before filing any applications or paying fees.

approvals.summary: The SoMa Youth and Family Special Use District requires Conditional Use Authorization for any restaurant use here, even though MUR zoning principally permits restaurants; formula retail is not decided because the description does not say whether the business is part of a chain.

findings.text: Planning Code Section 249.40A(c)(1)(A)(v) requires Conditional Use for a restaurant anywhere in the SoMa Youth and Family Special Use District, regardless of underlying zoning permissions, and 921 Folsom St is inside that district.
In MUR zoning without the special use district overlay, a restaurant is principally permitted under Planning Code Section 841 (the table row for retail sales and services).

The one Conditional Use Authorization for a restaurant in the Youth and Family SUD within the search area—276 5th St, filed April 2018—was approved November 2018, taking 229 days from filing to decision (N = 1).

The same 276 5th St address received an agency referral approval in July 2018 noting that on-site sale of alcohol requires CUA per the special use district, implying that restaurants without alcohol may have a different path.

The immediate block (915-917 Folsom, 21 m) has active restaurant uses with ABC Type 47 and Type 41 licenses and a multi-year history of restaurant approvals, showing established food-service character on this corridor.

The description does not state whether the business is part of a chain, so the rules could not decide whether formula retail controls apply; if it is formula retail, the Central SoMa SUD prohibits formula retail restaurants at this address.

approvals.summary: A health permit to operate is issued after plan check and inspection without a hearing; the application is referred to Planning for zoning review, which must resolve the conditional use question before DPH can issue the permit.

findings.text: Every food facility needs a health permit to operate, issued by the Department of Public Health after plan review, a pre-opening inspection and confirmation that a certified food safety manager is on staff.
The health permit application is sent to the Planning Department for zoning review under the interagency referral process, so Planning must approve the use before DPH issues the permit.

Health referrals for continuation of existing restaurant use in MUR were approved in under 30 days in comparable cases at 917 Folsom (27 days, February to March 2020) and at 915 Folsom (6 days, February 2018).

approvals.summary: A building permit is needed for tenant improvements and the kitchen build-out; a change of use from limited restaurant to restaurant is a Planning Code change of use, but whether it is also a Building Code change of occupancy is not established because the occupant load is not stated.

findings.text: The concept describes tenant improvements and upgrading to full cooking (hood, grills, fryers), which require a building permit with plans stamped by an architect and routed to DPH, Planning, Fire and Public Utilities for review.
Limited restaurant to restaurant is a Planning Code change of use, so the building permit is routed to Planning under Section 175 for zoning conformance before DBI issues it.

The Building Code classifies a restaurant or bar as Assembly Group A-2, and a space for fewer than 50 people as Group B; the description does not give the occupant load, so whether a change of occupancy is needed cannot be established.
No building permit, hood permit or health permit is on file at 921 Folsom St or the parcel in the records, so the existing kitchen equipment and its legal status are not shown by public records.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm in writing with Planning whether the change from limited restaurant to restaurant requires Conditional Use Authorization or qualifies as continuation under Section 841.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a zoning question to the SF Planning information desk or request a pre-application meeting, stating: '921 Folsom St, converting from limited restaurant to restaurant (full cooking, no alcohol, closing before midnight, not formula retail if independent). Does the Youth and Family SUD require CUA for this change, or is it approved as continuation of non-abandoned restaurant use under Section 841?' Attach a one-page concept summary, floor plan sketch and photos. Do not file a CUA application or pay fees until you have the answer in writing, because if it is continuation the path is a simple agency referral.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms CUA is required, file a Conditional Use Authorization application with the Planning Department, paying the application fee (about $3,100 for a use change with no new construction, subject to fee waiver programs).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Frame the application as an independent neighborhood restaurant upgrading cooking capabilities to serve the established SoMa food corridor, with no alcohol service, no late hours and a Good Neighbor Policy. Emphasize that 915-917 Folsom next door operate as restaurants with alcohol licenses, and that this concept is less intensive. Include a letter of support from the property owner, renderings of the interior, a sample menu, hours of operation (e.g., 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily) and a Good Neighbor Policy draft covering trash, noise, deliveries and a contact for complaints. The CUA will be scheduled for a Planning Commission hearing 3-6 months after filing, with 300-foot mailed notice and posted notice 30 days before the hearing.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation, $70-$150) and obtain a federal EIN from the IRS (free, same day online).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization for an LLC or Articles of Incorporation online at bizfile.sos.ca.gov, then apply for an EIN at irs.gov/EIN. The entity name and EIN are needed for the San Francisco business registration, bank account, lease signature and every other permit application.

filing_playbook.action: Register for a San Francisco Business Registration Certificate with the Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector ($55-$700 tiered by gross receipts, plus $4 state fee).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online at sftreasurer.org/business with the entity name, EIN, lease or location confirmation and principal officer information. The Business Account Number (BAN) issued is required for every City permit (health, building, sign, DBA). If the business is in a Priority Equity Geography (the address is inside that SUD), ask whether fee waivers under the First Year Free program apply.

filing_playbook.action: Submit building permit plans for tenant improvements and kitchen installation to the Department of Building Inspection, with architecture and MEP sheets routed to Planning, DPH, Fire and SFPUC.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Hire a licensed architect experienced in San Francisco restaurant build-outs to prepare plans showing the kitchen layout, hood and suppression system, grease interceptor, restrooms, hand sinks, ADA path of travel and finishes. Submit the DPH health plan check application at the same time the building permit is filed, listing the BAN, proposed menu, equipment schedule and finish schedule. Schedule a pre-submittal meeting with DPH Environmental Health to confirm the grease interceptor size, hand sink locations and three-compartment sink requirements before final plans. Building permit fees are a percentage of construction valuation, typically $800-$15,000; DPH plan check is $828-$2,207 flat fee depending on scope.

filing_playbook.action: During construction, obtain a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate (ServSafe or equivalent, $100-$250, valid 5 years) and ensure all food-handling employees complete California Food Handler training ($7-$15 per person, valid 3 years).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The owner or manager must pass an ANSI-accredited food safety exam within 60 days of opening; DPH asks for the certificate at the pre-opening inspection. Every employee who handles food must complete a Food Handler course within 30 days of hire. Keep copies on site for inspection.

filing_playbook.action: Before the final building inspection, schedule the Fire Department hood and suppression inspection and the DPH pre-opening inspection (at least two weeks' notice each).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Contact the SFFD Bureau of Fire Prevention to inspect the commercial hood suppression system and issue the fire permit (about $446 for a restaurant under 3,000 sq ft, plus hood plan review fees). Then schedule the DPH final inspection with the plan reviewer assigned to the project, confirming hot water, hand sinks, sealed surfaces and the food safety manager certificate are ready. DPH issues the Permit to Operate (application fee $470, annual license $0 for 2026-28) after the final inspection passes.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a California Seller's Permit (free, CDTFA online) for sales tax, register as an employer with EDD (free, online) for payroll taxes, and secure workers' compensation insurance before the first employee starts.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply for the Seller's Permit at onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov; it is required before opening and often requested by suppliers. Register with EDD e-Services for Business within 15 days of the first payroll; your payroll provider needs the EDD account number. Quote workers' comp insurance through a broker or State Fund (premiums are 2-6 percent of payroll for restaurant class codes); DPH and other departments may ask for proof of coverage.

timeline_cost.notes: This range is the time to obtain approval of the Conditional Use Authorization, the health permit and the building permit with change of use, when those approvals are granted. The 120-300 day span reflects the CUA critical path: the one comparable CUA in the Youth and Family SUD took 229 days from filing to Commission approval (April to November 2018), and typical CUA timelines including pre-application meetings, environmental review, noticing and hearing scheduling run 6-10 months. If Planning confirms in writing that the change qualifies as continuation under Section 841 instead of a new CUA, the timeline collapses to 60-120 days (the building permit and health plan check) and the $3,100 CUA fee is avoided. Government cost includes the CUA application fee (about $3,150 in 2023, CPI-adjusted from the 2023-24 schedule), building permit fees ($800-$15,000 depending on construction valuation), DPH plan check ($828-$2,207) and health permit application ($470), plus business registration ($55-$700), fire permit (about $446) and other ministerial fees. The range excludes construction costs, architect and expediter fees, and any appeal period or revision time. It is a time to approval; if the CUA is denied or the application is withdrawn, no timeline or cost is given.
